steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

tools.description:
Login



The "No Contact" Reinforcement
Tool • Gate: Heartbreak Loop
tools.summary: The "No Contact" Reinforcement helps you. This practice supports emotional regulation and practical problem-solving. Use it when you need a clear, structured approach to manage difficult feelings or situations.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

tools.summary: The Partner Empowerment Tool helps you. This practice supports emotional regulation and practical problem-solving. Use it when you need a clear, structured approach to manage difficult feelings or situations.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.

Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)

Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

tools.title: Thought Unhook
tools.description: Create distance from looping thoughts. This practice helps you observe your thoughts without getting caught in them, reducing the intensity of repetitive thinking patterns.
tools.summary: Create distance from looping thoughts.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Notice a thought that's looping or causing distress.
Say to yourself: 'I'm having the thought that...' (complete with your actual thought).
Notice that you are not the thought itself—you are the one observing it.
Imagine the thought as a cloud passing in the sky, or words on a screen.
Take a breath and let the thought be there without fighting it or getting pulled into it.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a comfortable seated position.
Close your eyes and take a few deep breaths.
Notice what thoughts are present right now, without judgment.
When you notice a thought that's looping or causing distress, practice 'unhooking':
- Name it: 'I'm having the thought that...'
- Notice where you feel it in your body.
- Imagine the thought as an object you can observe (a cloud, a leaf on a stream, words on a screen).
- Thank your mind for the thought, then gently return your attention to your breath.
Continue this practice for 10-15 minutes, unhooking from thoughts as they arise.
When finished, take a moment to notice how you feel.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set up your practice space and settle into a comfortable position.
Begin with 5 minutes of breath awareness to center yourself.
Practice the 'Leaves on a Stream' visualization: Imagine your thoughts as leaves floating down a stream. Watch them come and go without holding onto them.
For each thought that arises:
- Acknowledge it: 'There's a thought about...'
- Notice its emotional charge and where you feel it in your body.
- Practice defusion: See the thought as separate from you, as words or images you're observing.
- Choose your response: Do you need to act on this thought, or can you let it pass?
Explore the difference between thoughts and facts. Ask: 'Is this thought helpful right now?'
Practice self-compassion: Your mind is trying to help, even when thoughts feel unhelpful.
Spend the final 10 minutes in open awareness, observing thoughts as they come and go.
Reflect on what you learned about your thought patterns and how unhooking felt.

tools.howWhyWorks: Thought unhooking (also called cognitive defusion) is based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). It works by helping you see thoughts as mental events rather than absolute truths. This creates psychological distance, reducing the power thoughts have over your emotions and behavior. Research shows that defusion techniques can reduce the distress caused by repetitive negative thoughts.

citations.source: Hayes, S. C., Strosahl, K. D., & Wilson, K. G. (2011). Acceptance and Commitment Therapy: The Process and Practice of Mindful Change.

tools.title: Trauma‑Informed Grounding
tools.description:
Login



Trauma‑Informed Grounding
Tool • Gate: Grief & Loss
tools.summary: Trauma‑Informed Grounding helps you. This practice supports emotional regulation and practical problem-solving. Use it when you need a clear, structured approach to manage difficult feelings or situations.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

tools.howWhyWorks: Trauma‑Informed Grounding works by providing structure when things feel overwhelming. Breaking challenges into smaller steps makes them more manageable. Taking concrete actions, even small ones, helps shift from feeling stuck to making progress. This approach is grounded in behavioral activation and cognitive restructuring, which show that action and perspective shifts can improve emotional well-being.

Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.

tools.summary: Weekly Check‑In Ritual helps you. This practice supports emotional regulation and practical problem-solving. Use it when you need a clear, structured approach to manage difficult feelings or situations.

walkthroughs.title: Quick Workthrough (5 min)
steps: Take a moment to pause and notice what you're experiencing right now.
Identify one specific thing you can do in the next few minutes.
Take that action, even if it's small.
Notice how you feel after taking the step.
Acknowledge what you've done, no matter how small it seems.

walkthroughs.title: Standard Workthrough (15 min)
steps: Find a quiet space where you can focus for about 15 minutes.
Take three slow breaths, noticing the air moving in and out.
Identify the specific challenge or feeling you're working with.
Break it down into smaller, manageable pieces.
Choose one piece to address right now.
Decide on a concrete action you can take.
Take that action, paying attention to what happens.
Reflect on what you learned from taking the step.
Notice any shifts in how you feel.
Plan one next step for later today or tomorrow.

walkthroughs.title: Deep Workthrough (30 min)
steps: Set aside 30 minutes in a space where you won't be interrupted.
Begin with five minutes of quiet breathing, letting your body settle.
Identify the core issue you want to work with today.
Explore what this issue means to you personally.
Notice any patterns or connections to past experiences.
Break the issue into its component parts.
Examine each part with curiosity rather than judgment.
Identify what's within your control and what isn't.
Choose one aspect you can influence right now.
Develop a specific plan of action.
Take the first step of your plan.
Observe what happens, both internally and externally.
Reflect on what you learned from this process.
Identify what you'll do differently going forward.
Acknowledge your effort and commitment to working through this.
